To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the price of a convertible bond can be computed as the solution of a reflected BSDE, that the price is the viscosity solution of the associated variational inequality, and that the price is a smooth function of the underlying stock.

(i) a doubly reflected BSDE is the natural framework for super-hedging a convertible security; (ii) this BSDE has a solution; and (iii) the solution can be characterized by a viscosity solution of a variational inequality.

1. the arbitrage value (AV) of a CS can be super-hedged by a self-financing portfolio of the underlying assets; 2. the AV of a CS can also be super-hedgerd by a game exchange option (GEO) strategy; 3. the AV of CS is equal to the value of the GEO strategy; 4. the AV of the CS can also be characterized as a viscosity solution of a system of variational inequalities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the valuation and hedging of convertible bonds in a model where default and credit spread are explicitly considered.
the pricing and hedging of convertible bonds in a defaultable market.
the study of the pricing of a convertible bond (or a more general convertible security) and the hedging of its arbitrage value in a defaultable diffusion model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CS market is not a zero sum game.
convertible bonds can be priced and hedged by the issuer and the holder, and this is done in a consistent and coherent way.

, in the present setup, the arbitrage value (or price) of a CS can be hedged at the same initial price for both issuer and investor, and the arbitrage value can be characterized in terms of viscosity solution of a variational inequality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide an explicit pricing and hedging framework for CSs in the case of defaultable assets, in a primary market context.
we provide an analytical framework for pricing CS in presence of default risk and we show the existence of a super-hedging strategy in the same setting.
, in a primary market setup, the value of convertible bonds can be hedged by a combination of a rolling CDS, a straight bond, and the game exchange option.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of default in our market model does not prevent the existence and uniqueness of a solution to the associated doubly reflected backward stochastic differential equation, which is a necessary condition for the existence of super-hedging strategies for the arbitrage value process of a convertible security.

the presence of the CDS contract in the market allows to price a CS in a consistent way, in the sense that the price of a convertible bond is a supermartingale under the CDS contract default probability.
the value of a convertible bond can be decomposed in terms of a game exchange option and a straight bond.
